# Starting with the pi Analysis #
```{bash}
# Made a new directory for the HW Analysis
'/users/s/r/srhousto/SydHoustonEcoGenomics/PopulationGenomics/mydata/pi100kb'
```

# Calculating pi for the Northernmost (KRU) and Southernmost (ASU) Populations in 100kb (100,000 bases) windows
```{bash}
# WINDOW changed from 10,000 to 100,000
WINDOW=100000 

for KEEP in pops/KRU.txt pops/ASU.txt; do
    POP=$(basename $KEEP .txt)
    echo "== $POP =="
    vcftools --gzvcf $VCF \
        --keep $KEEP \
        --window-pi $WINDOW \
        --out pi100kb/$POP
done

# Checking the output
ls pi100kb
# ASU.log  ASU.windowed.pi  KRU.log  KRU.windowed.pi
```

# average the latitudes so we can ordering the sites north to south
```{r}
meta <- read_csv("mydata/sample_metadata.csv")

sites <- meta %>%
  group_by(Population) %>%
  summarise(Latitude = mean(Latitude))
```

# Reading the files generated from bash earlier, "ASU.windowed.pi" and "KRU.windowed.pi" that are in the new pi100kb folder
```{r}
pi_files <- list.files("mydata/pi100kb", pattern = "windowed.pi$", full.names = TRUE)
pi_files
```

#Renaming each file so its site is just its name (ex. "ASU" and "KRU"), then reading all the files and stacking then and putting the names generated before in a new coloumn called 'Site'
```{r}
pi <- pi_files %>%
  set_names(str_remove(basename(pi_files), fixed(".windowed.pi"))) %>%
  map_dfr(read_tsv, .id = "Population", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  left_join(sites, by = "Population") %>%
  mutate(Site = fct_reorder(Population, Latitude))
```

# Summarize pi for each site
```{r}
pi_summary <- pi %>%
  group_by(Population, Latitude) %>%
  summarise(n_windows = n(),
            mean_pi   = mean(PI),
            median_pi = median(PI),
            .groups = "drop")
pi_summary

# ASU Mean = 0.0007231196
# ASU Median = 0.0002478065
# KRU Mean = 0.0005898773
# KRU Median = 0.0001971280
```

# I tried to make a whole genome pi plot, first by altering the scaffold code to include all the data and not just the top scaffold, and then by altering the FST scan code to plot it like a scatterplot, but both plots were too messy overall because there were too many points and i decided it was better to just use a violin plot alongside the mean and median data. 

```{r}
# From the FST section : 
add_genome_pos <- function(df) {
  scaffolds <- df %>% 
    group_by(CHROM) %>% ##group by CHROM
    summarise(length = max(POS)) %>% ## length = max position within a chromosome
    arrange(match(CHROM, unique(df$CHROM))) %>% ##make sure each is unique, arranged
    mutate(offset = cumsum(as.numeric(length)) - length, ###cumulatively number (helps with labels)
           shade  = factor(row_number() %% 2))    ##value for alternating colour 
  df %>%
    left_join(scaffolds, by = "CHROM") %>% ##join this data by given data with CHROM
    mutate(genome_pos = offset + POS) ###cumalative genome pos 
}
```

### Identifying outliers with Fst ###

### Bash ### 

# Made a fst100kb folder in mydata '/users/s/r/srhousto/SydHoustonEcoGenomics/PopulationGenomics/mydata/fst100kb'

```{bash}
cd $DATA_DIR

module load gcc
module load vcftools

VCF=$DATA_DIR/Lottia_gigantea_pl_flt3.renamed.vcf.gz
```

# Testing the most southern and the most northern populations
```{bash}
POP1=ASU
POP2=KRU
```

# Genome-Wide Fst between 2 populations
```{bash}
vcftools --gzvcf ${VCF} \
  --weir-fst-pop pops/${POP1}.txt \
  --weir-fst-pop pops/${POP2}.txt \
  --out fst/${POP1}_vs_${POP2} \
  2> fst100kb/${POP1}_vs_${POP2}.log
  
# "ASU_vs_KRU.log"
```

# Now Using a window size of 100,000 bases
```{bash}
vcftools --gzvcf ${VCF} \
  --weir-fst-pop pops/${POP1}.txt \
  --weir-fst-pop pops/${POP2}.txt \
  --fst-window-size 100000 \
  --fst-window-step 100000 \
  --out fst100kb/${POP1}_vs_${POP2}_FST_100kb \
  2> fst100kb/${POP1}_vs_${POP2}_FST_100kb.log

# "ASU_vs_KRU_FST_100kb.log"
```


```{r}
add_genome_pos <- function(df) {
  scaffolds <- df %>% 
    group_by(CHROM) %>% 
    summarise(length = max(POS)) %>% ## length = max position within a chromosome
    arrange(match(CHROM, unique(df$CHROM))) %>% ##make sure each is unique, arranged
    mutate(offset = cumsum(as.numeric(length)) - length, ###cumulatively number (helps with labels)
           shade  = factor(row_number() %% 2))    ##value for alternating colour 
  df %>%
    left_join(scaffolds, by = "CHROM") %>% ##join this data by given data with CHROM
    mutate(genome_pos = offset + POS) ###cumalative genome pos 
}

fst_win <- fst_win %>%
  mutate(POS = (BIN_START + BIN_END) / 2) %>% 
  add_genome_pos() ## this is our new function

```

```{r}
# empirical outlier threshold: the top 1% of windows
fst_cut <- quantile(fst_win$WEIGHTED_FST, probs = 0.99)
fst_cut

fst_win <- mutate(fst_win, outlier = WEIGHTED_FST >= fst_cut)

ggplot(fst_win, aes(x = genome_pos / 1e6, y = WEIGHTED_FST)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = shade), size = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = filter(fst_win, outlier), colour = "red", size = 1.2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = fst_cut, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("grey35", "grey70"), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Position along the genome (Mb; scaffolds end to end)",
       y = "Weighted FST (100-kb windows)",
       title = paste(pop1, "vs", pop2)) +
  theme_classic()

ggsave(paste0(OUTDIR, "/fst100kb/fst_scan_", pop1, "_vs_", pop2, "_100kb.png"),
       width = 10, height = 4)
```

# Started with Linkage Pruning

```{bash}
# Made a new folder called popstructure100kb in myresults
DATA_DIR=/gpfs1/home/s/r/srhousto/SydHoustonEcoGenomics/PopulationGenomics/mydata
VCF=$DATA_DIR/Lottia_gigantea_pl_flt3.renamed.vcf.gz
module load plink
plink --version
#v1.9.0-b.7.7
```

# Using plink to prune the data (try to eliminate linked SNPs), changed to the 100kb window
```{bash}
plink --vcf $VCF --double-id --allow-extra-chr \
  --set-missing-var-ids @:# \
  --indep-pairwise 100kb 1 0.2 \
  --out Lg_LD_100kb
  
# Original SNPs: 1,821,750
# SNPs removed: 1,296,627
# SNPs kept: 525,123
```

# Making the PCA
```{bash}
plink --vcf $VCF --double-id --allow-extra-chr --set-missing-var-ids @:# \
  --extract Lg_LD_100kb.prune.in \
  --make-bed --pca --out Lg_LD_100kb
  
# 553 individuals included across all populations.
# Output = Lg_LD_100kb.eigenvec and Lg_LD_100kb.eigenval
```

### R ### 

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
setwd('~/SydHoustonEcoGenomics/PopulationGenomics/mydata')

# the .eigenvec file has no column names, so col_names = FALSE (they become X1, X2, ...)
pca <- read_table("mydata/Lg_LD_100kb.eigenvec", col_names = FALSE)

# the .eigenval file is just a list of numbers, so scan() reads it into a vector
eigenval <- scan("mydata/Lg_LD_100kb.eigenval")

# columns 1 and 2 are the family and individual IDs, which are identical
# thanks to --double-id, so drop column 2 (remember: [rows, columns])
pca <- pca[, -2]

# rename the columns: the first is the sample ID, the rest are PC1, PC2, ...
# paste0() joins text and numbers, e.g. paste0("PC", 1:3) gives "PC1" "PC2" "PC3"
names(pca)[1] <- "ID"
names(pca)[2:ncol(pca)] <- paste0("PC", 1:(ncol(pca) - 1))

head(pca)
```

```{r}
meta <- read_csv("mydata/sample_metadata.csv")
# Adding the metadata to the PCA results
pca <- left_join(pca, meta, by = "ID")
sum(is.na(pca$Site))
# Prints 0 (makes sure everyone is matched correctly)
```

# Calculating PVE

```{r}
# convert the eigenvalues to a percentage variance explained (pve)
pve <- data.frame(PC = seq_along(eigenval),
                  pve = eigenval / sum(eigenval) * 100)

# make a folder for our figures

pve_plot <- ggplot(pve, aes(PC, pve)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(x = "Principal component", y = "Percentage variance explained") +
  theme_bw()
pve_plot

OUTDIR="~/SydHoustonEcoGenomics/PopulationGenomics/myresults/popstructure100kb"

ggsave(pve_plot, file=paste0(OUTDIR, "/variance_0.2_100kb.png"), width = 6, height = 4)
```

# Doing XtX but with the full dataset not the subsetted one

## Starting w Xtx
```{r}
# Copied over the file Lottia_bp_2_summary_pi_xtx.out from the BaypassHomework file in terminal, it is now located in mydata

# 4.6

snps <- read_tsv("mydata/baypass/Lottia.baypass.snps.txt")

snps$MRK<-rownames(snps)
snps$MRK<-as.numeric(snps$MRK)

npop <- 19

# Same as before but with the new file 
xtx <- read.table("mydata/Lottia_bp_2_summary_pi_xtx.out", header = TRUE, check.names = FALSE) %>%
  left_join(snps, by = "MRK") %>%
  mutate(lp_high   = pchisq(XtXst, npop, lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE),   #
         lp_low    = pchisq(XtXst, npop, lower.tail = TRUE,  log.p = TRUE),   
         direction = if_else(lp_high < lp_low, "high", "low"),
         log10_p   = -(pmin(lp_high, lp_low) + log(2)) / log(10),             
         pval      = 10^(-log10_p),
         qval      = p.adjust(pval, method = "BH"))
```

# Top GO

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(topGO)

outlier_file <- "mydata/HWbaypass_xtx_outliers.txt"
map_file <- "mydata/100kbGO/lottia_gene2GO.map"
snp2gene_file <- "mydata/100kbGO/lottia_snp2gene_genic.tsv" 

###read in GO terms 
gene2GO <- readMappings(map_file)
length(gene2GO)          # how many genes have at least one GO term? - 13710
gene2GO[1:2]             # what does an entry look like?

##creating the gene universe - all genes in experiment 
snp2gene <- read.delim(snp2gene_file, header = FALSE,
                       col.names = c("CHROM", "POS", "GeneId"))
universe <- unique(snp2gene$GeneId)
length(universe) # 21314

mean(universe %in% names(gene2GO))    # proportion of universe genes with GO terms
# 0.592709

## Genes that contain at least one outlier SNP.
outliers   <- read.table(outlier_file, header = TRUE)
hits       <- merge(outliers[, c("CHROM", "POS")], snp2gene, by = c("CHROM", "POS"))
candidates <- unique(hits$GeneId)

##how many candiate genes do we have?
cat("Outlier SNPs:", nrow(outliers),
    "| outlier SNPs inside genes:", nrow(unique(hits[, c("CHROM", "POS")])),
    "| candidate genes:", length(candidates), "\n")

# Outlier SNPs: 1822 | outlier SNPs inside genes: 699 | candidate genes: 267

geneList <- factor(as.integer(universe %in% candidates), levels = c(0, 1))
names(geneList) <- universe
table(geneList)
geneList 
# 0 = background 1 = candidate genes
#    0     1 
# 21047   267 

## nodeSize = 10 ignores GO terms with fewer than 10 annotated genes (we can add a max here if we have very broad terms), keeping 10
GOdata <- new("topGOdata",
              ontology = "BP", ##biological processes, what about other options?
              allGenes = geneList,
              annot    = annFUN.gene2GO,
              gene2GO  = gene2GO,
              nodeSize = 10)
GOdata
# 267 from array, 107 can be used in analysis

## Test for enrichment 
result <- runTest(GOdata, algorithm = "weight01", statistic = "fisher")
result
#  Annotated genes: 8897 
#  Significant genes: 107 
#  Min. no. of genes annotated to a GO: 10 
#  Nontrivial nodes: 618 
```

## Results table

```{r}
## Annotated   = universe genes in the term
## Significant = candidate genes in the term
## Expected    = candidates expected by chance
res <- GenTable(GOdata, weight01 = result, orderBy = "weight01",
                topNodes = 50, numChar = 1000)
res$p <- as.numeric(sub("< ", "", res$weight01))   
head(res, 10)


##write our outliers
write.csv(res, "topGO_BP_HWxtx.csv", row.names = FALSE)

## Which candidate genes are in the top term?
top_term <- res$GO.ID[1]
intersect(genesInTerm(GOdata, top_term)[[1]], sigGenes(GOdata))

## GeneRatio = candidate genes in the term / all candidates with GO terms
plot_df <- subset(res, p < 0.05)
if (nrow(plot_df) == 0) {
  message("No terms with p < 0.05 - plotting the top 15 anyway (none significant)")
  plot_df <- head(res, 15)
}
plot_df <- head(plot_df, 20)
plot_df$GeneRatio <- plot_df$Significant / numSigGenes(GOdata)
plot_df$logP      <- -log10(plot_df$p)
## wrap long GO term names over two lines so the text doesn't dominate the plot
plot_df$Label <- vapply(plot_df$Term, function(t) paste(strwrap(t, width = 40), collapse = "\n"),
                        character(1))
plot_df$Label <- reorder(plot_df$Label, plot_df$GeneRatio)

p1 <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Label, y = GeneRatio, size = Significant, fill = logP)) +
  geom_segment(aes(y = 0, yend = GeneRatio, x = Label, xend = Label),
               colour = "lightblue", linewidth = 1.5, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, alpha = 0.8, colour = "black") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 4)) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(colour = "black", lineheight = 0.9),
        plot.title.position = "plot",
        panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = c("#2b83ba", "#fdae61", "#d7191c"),
                       name = "-log10(p value)") +
  scale_size(range = c(3, 10), name = "Count") +
  ylab("Gene Ratio") + xlab("")


ggsave("topGO_BP_HW100kb2.png", p1,
       width = 9, height = max(4, 1 + 0.42 * nrow(plot_df)), dpi = 300)
```
